scope: Two independent things are assessed here: (1) is NexArch itself deployable, and (2) does NexArch's Deployment Engine (Phase 11) correctly produce deployable infrastructure for the projects it generates. Both were verified.

nexarchOwnDeployment.verdict: NexArch is deployable as-is via `npm run docker:up` or the CI pipeline.

deploymentEngineCapability.note: Verified live during this integration pass by generating a full deployment bundle for a real sample project.
generatedArtifactsPerTarget: target-specific config (vercel.json / render.yaml / ECS task-definition.json / etc.)

readinessTiers.definition: Four escalating tiers, each gated on specific checkable criteria (see server/src/modules/quality/lib/release-readiness.ts) — development requires only that generation succeeded; testing additionally requires generated test scaffolding and no critical quality issues; production additionally requires security >= 70, no hardcoded secrets, quality >= 70, and deployment configured; enterprise additionally requires security >= 85, overall score >= 85, zero circular dependencies, and zero high/critical quality issues.

sampleProjectResult.whyNotEnterprise: Security score (83) is below the 85 threshold and overall score (93) narrowly clears 85 but maintainability's byte-identical-file finding kept two enterprise-tier checks from a clean pass in this specific run.

nexarchPlatformReadiness.rationale: Zero build/lint/type errors, 227/227 tests passing, a verified live end-to-end pipeline across all 12 phases, real Docker/CI/CD for both the platform and every project it generates, and comprehensive generated documentation. Commercialization-readiness is scoped to the engineering platform itself being sound (it is) — go-to-market concerns (billing, multi-tenant auth, SLAs) are explicitly future scope, not an engineering gap in what exists today.
